root_idea.summary: Classical root analysis distinguishes three semantic branches: becoming thin or emaciated, giving, and claiming or adopting something as one's own.
root_idea.development: A proposed derivation connects the gift branch with the bee's beneficial giving. The thinness branch extends from an emaciated body to thin sword edges; these developments do not merge the distinct lexical branches.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular noun citation form.
Displayed under the normalized noun citation form for the bee.

senses.definition: A freely bestowed gift or donation; in Qur'an 4:4, the bridal gift or dower given to women as a free and willing bestowal.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the construction وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً, characterizing the giving as voluntary and without seeking an exchange.
The noun denotes the specified bee in the Quranic account of God's inspiration to it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thin, lean, or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said especially of the body; the same thinness is reflected in the term for thin-edged swords.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or bestow something as a free gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The giving is understood as voluntary and without seeking compensation; the usage includes giving a gift to a person such as a child or wife.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prescribed obligation or religious duty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Arabic sense distinct from the voluntary-gift use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A religion, creed, or religious affiliation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as مَا نِحْلَتُكَ, meaning “What is your religion?”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin-edged swords whose blade edges have become thin through repeated striking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived plural description based on the thinness of the sword edges.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To claim or adopt something as one's own, including poetry or another literary production.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two forms are treated as equivalent here; a proposed distinction between rightful and wrongful claiming is not established.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit's meaning of becoming lean or emaciated is represented.
The unit's obligation and religion senses are represented separately.

cautions: نِحْلَة, the free-gift or dower term, and نَحْل, the bee, are distinct Quranic lexical items despite sharing the consonantal root.
The obligation and religion senses of نِحْلَة are Classical Arabic meanings and are not treated as the meaning of the Quranic dower usage in this packet.
